summary: Protect new assistant pairing codes from offline guessing with the member-local keyed verifier bound to the stored assistant grant ID.

replay.detail: No claim replay or rebuild. Completed assistant grants remain usable. Pending unmarked legacy challenges are accepted only while unexpired and when challenge expiry minus BEGUN accepted_at_unix_ms is at most 300000 ms.

schema.detail: New custom.client.assistant.v1.begun claims add verifier: hmac-sha256-v1 and verifier_key_id: SHA256(secret); code_hash stores HMAC-SHA-256 instead of an unkeyed code digest. MAC input is the domain bytes fractal/pairing-code-verifier/v1 (no NUL), the stored BEGUN grant_id including its assistant-grant/ prefix, then the code's UTF-8 bytes, each prefixed by its byte length as an unsigned big-endian u32, without normalization. Completion uses the stored grant ID, not the request's bare pairing ID. GRANTED removes verifier, verifier_key_id, code_hash and challenge_expires_at_unix_ms. No database schema version or closed registry declaration changes; these historical custom claims have open fields. Bearer credential_digest/credential_hash storage and authentication are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Assistant pairing request and response shapes are unchanged. Unknown or malformed verifier markers, missing or replaced secrets, mismatched verifier_key_id, or an overlong legacy challenge lifetime return HTTP 403 pairing-restart-required with message start pairing again. There is no legacy digest fallback when the verifier marker is present. Refusal does not change BEGUN or write GRANTED, credentials or completion state; the denied-completion audit retains denial_code pairing-restart-required. Incorrect codes with the matching key retain forbidden. Replicated claims alone do not permit offline guessing against new keyed verifiers; code entropy, the five-minute lifetime, single-use enforcement and encrypted transport requirements are unchanged.

downtime.detail: No restart-time migration or rebuild. Ordinary restarts retaining the same member-local secret preserve live pending challenges.

manual.detail: The verifier secret shared by person and assistant pairing remains at state_dir/pairing-verifier/key with mode 0600 and parent directory mode 0700. Keep it private: it is not replicated in claims and is excluded from logical claim backups. After a claim-only restore or secret loss or replacement, start pending pairings again on the intended member; retrying an old code cannot recover the challenge. Binary downgrade: older binaries compare keyed code_hash against the unkeyed code digest and refuse pending keyed challenges as invalid rather than pairing-restart-required. Begin those pairings again on the downgraded member. Completed grants require no migration.

recovery.detail: Start fresh pairing after a claim-only restore, verifier-secret loss or replacement, unknown or malformed verifier marker, or an overlong legacy challenge lifetime. There is intentionally no rollback protection when both the original secret and claims are restored to an earlier state: a previously consumed challenge may become usable again until its original expiry. Such a restore does not preserve single-use history.
